# Sinai's generator theorem, noninvertible case

Let $T$ be a measure-preserving transformation of a probability space $(X, \mathcal{B}, \mu)$, not
necessarily invertible, and let $\xi = \{C_1, \dots, C_r\}$ be a finite measurable partition which is a
*strong generator*: the σ-algebra generated by the sets $T^{-i} C_j$, $i \ge 0$, is $\mathcal{B}$ modulo
$\mu$. Then $h_\mu(T) = h_\mu(T, \xi)$.

This is the form used for one-sided shifts, where the partition into 1-cylinders is a strong generator;
compare the [invertible statement](ks-entropy-eq-entropy-rel-of-is-generato.md). The statement is wanted.

## Sources

- O. Sarig, *Lecture Notes on Ergodic Theory*, Definition 4.4 (strong generator) and Theorem 4.4, whose
  statement covers noninvertible maps with a strong generator.
